in, a preposition constructed with the dative, with local meaning, of persons and things being in some place.

ἐν [in] in expressions signifying time
ἐν [in] is often placed where the Latins say inter, as ἐν βροτοῖς [among mortals] inter mortales.
ἐν [in] of things in which something is perceived
ἐν [in] towards, as regards
ἐν [in] is not rarely placed where the instrumental dative without ἐν would have been used.
ἐν [in] used adverbially with the particle δέ, ἐν δέ, i.e. among others or among other things

Very frequent are ἐν δόμοις [in the houses] Pers. 776. Ag. 606, 964, 971, 1102, 1189, 1313, 1397, 1460, 1492. Ch. 101, 349, 537, 554, 662, 698, 745, 805, 1005. Eum. 723. Fr. 321. ἐν δώμασιν [in the halls] Ag. 773. Ch. 36. ἐν πύλαις [at the gates] Sept. 160, 213, 249, 376, 451, 958. ἐν πυλώμασιν [in the gateways] 799. ἐν γῇ or γαίᾳ [in the earth] Sept. 567, 937. Eum. 781, 811. Suppl. 834. ἐν χθονί [in the ground] Pers. 482. Ag. 506. Suppl. 242, 829, 858. ἐν πόλει [in the city] Sept. 1009. Ag. 321. Eum. 776. ἐν τόποις [in places] Pers. 796. Ag. 191. Eum. 706. Suppl. 50. ἐν χεροῖν or ἐν χερσίν [in the hands] Sept. 473. Ch. 160. Fr. 55. ἐν φρενί or ἐν φρεσίν [in the mind] Sept. 25. Pers. 165. Ag. 1084. Ch. 450, 704. ἐν κακοῖς [in evils], about which will be said below. The rest, collected and correctly arranged by Wellauer, are these:
